goal: An arithmetic equation (a op b = result) is laid out on pads with exactly one number or operator missing; pick the correct missing digit or operator tile from the loose tiles on the table, place it on the empty pad, and bring the arms home.
instruction_templates: Complete the equation by selecting the correct missing number or operator and placing it on the pad, then reset the robot arm.
success: Let M be the missing equation slot (t0, t1 (operator), t2, t4, or t5 when the result has two digits) and mat_M its pad; the candidate set is every loose tile that would make the equation true: digit tiles num_0..num_9 whose digit (model index mod 10) completes a valid equation (for t1 candidates are the operator tiles plus/minus/multiplication/division). Validity: t0 op t2 = result, result = t4 (one digit) or 10*t4 + t5 (when a t5 slot exists); minus requires a - b >= 0, division requires b != 0 and a divisible by b (integer division); several candidates can be valid (e.g. 4 ? 2 = 2 is true for minus and division).
Position: some candidate tile has its root XY within 0.018 m (strict) of the root XY of the pad mat_M.
Orientation 1: some candidate tile's local +X axis is within 45 deg (strict) of world +X.
Orientation 2: some candidate tile's local +Y axis is within 45 deg (strict) of world +Y.

Both target arms back at origin: all target arms (left_arm and right_arm; the support arm is not counted) have their end-effector pose within 0.15 m on EACH axis (|dx|,|dy|,|dz| all <= 0.15 m) and within 20 degrees (quaternion angle) of the pose they had at the start of the episode (recorded after the scene settled).

All of the above hold simultaneously after one action (note the three 'some candidate' conditions are evaluated independently, so with several valid candidates they could be satisfied by different tiles).
evaluation: Single stage (one list of 4 conditions, each of the first three being an OR over the valid candidate tiles), checked after every action. The reward manager is evaluated only once per action (after the sim sub-steps of that action are finished), never between sub-steps. In each evaluation the FIRST pending stage of the check list is tested (every condition in it, all at that same moment; a condition that is a nested list is an OR); when it passes it is removed permanently (never re-verified later) and the next stage becomes pending; at most one stage is removed per action. Reward is 1.0 only when the check list is empty (and no query/trigger counter is violated); the episode is declared a success as soon as reward >= 0.999 after an action, and ends as a failure if the action counter reaches step_lim without that, or earlier if the environment is flagged failed (query counter exceeded, see below). No final_check list is registered by this task, so the final-check logic at step_lim adds nothing. No early failure condition; wrong tiles placed on the pad are not penalised as long as a valid tile satisfies the conditions at some action.
objects: mat0..mat4 (and mat5 when the result has two digits): square pads ('cube_cushion', Geometry static), table-frame y=0.0, x = -0.17, -0.085, 0.0, 0.085, 0.17 (mat5 at x=0.255, added only by the layout sampler for two-digit results)

t0, t2, t4 (and t5): the equation's digits shown on mat0, mat2, mat4 (mat5) (Rigid 'number' tiles, any digit 0-9); t1: the operator tile (plus, minus, division or multiplication) shown on mat1; the slot that is the missing one is NOT present in the scene (removed by the external layout sampler, not by the yml)
equal: an equals-sign tile placed on mat3

num_0..num_9: ten loose digit tiles (Rigid 'number' category, one for each digit 0-9; digit = model index mod 10, three look variants per digit), table-frame x in [-0.43,0.43], y in [-0.27,0.0], random yaw up to +-45 deg, margin 0.005
plus, minus, multiplication, division: four loose operator tiles (Rigid), fixed table-frame y=-0.27 and x = -0.15, -0.05, 0.05, 0.15 respectively, no rotation
needs_memory_or_language: Yes (visual): read the equation on the pads (digits and operator) and solve it to find which tile is missing; read the loose tiles (digit appearance) to find the right one. The result may be two digits. Language only generic.
end_requirements: Both arms within 0.15 m per axis and 20 deg of their start pose at the same action in which the tile is on the pad with the right orientation.
notes: The yml lists t0,t1,t2,t4 (always) but the reward code requires exactly one of the equation slots (among t0,t1,t2,t4,t5) to be absent; the yml shown is a template and the actual layout (equation values, missing slot, optional mat5/t5) comes from an external layout sampler. Statically it cannot be determined which slot is missing or what the equation is. The answer may be unique or ambiguous (several valid tiles). Orientation tolerance: tile must not be rotated more than 45 deg about its vertical axis from the world axes (+X and +Y of the tile within 45 deg of world +X and +Y), and not flipped or heavily tilted. Position tolerance 1.8 cm is tight relative to the pad size (pad spacing 8.5 cm). Placing the right tile with wrong yaw (>45 deg), or leaving arms away from home, fails. A candidate tile that is also the digit already used in the equation is a different object (loose tiles are separate).
